name: Open World Clock
description: The best world clock for Windows. Completely free, no strings attached. Open source (MIT), for Windows 10 and 11. Day and night cards follow each city's real sunrise and sunset; a time zone converter and mouse-wheel time scrubber move every clock at once; a meeting planner shows the hours everyone is at work; a world map shows day and night live. No price, no ads, no account, no telemetry, and it works offline.
applicationSubCategory: World clock, time zone converter and meeting planner

subjectOf.name: How to show multiple time zones on Windows 11 and 10

potentialAction.description: Install from the Microsoft Store (x64 and ARM64, updates itself), or run: winget install 9N88FR8M81BM -s msstore. The x64 installer (per user, no admin rights) and portable exe are at https://download.openworldclock.com/Open-World-Clock-1.3.0-setup.exe and https://download.openworldclock.com/Open-World-Clock-1.3.0-portable.exe.

featureList: Always-on-top world clock for Windows 10 and 11
Day and night cards from each city's real sunrise and sunset, calculated offline
Time zone converter: type 9:30, 3pm or 15h30 in any city
+1 day and -1 day markers when the date changes
Likely asleep cue for cities between 22:00 and 07:00
Time scrubber: mouse wheel, day-line drag or keyboard, in 15-minute steps
Meeting planner with working hours and workdays per city and an overlap band
World map view with live day and night
Clock-change notes before daylight saving time starts or ends
Search by city, country, abbreviation (EST) or UTC offset (UTC-5)
Custom city labels
Copy converted times as text, as Discord timestamps or in UTC, or save a calendar invite (.ics)
Strip, compact and vertical layouts
Windows 11 Snap and native acrylic backdrop
Light, dark and system themes with adjustable opacity
12 or 24-hour clock, optional seconds
English, Portuguese and Spanish
Keyboard and screen reader support
No account, no ads, no telemetry, works offline
Free and open source (MIT License)
